title: Doing: Making the Best Action Choices
coreMove: Choose the next action by filtering a trusted list through context, time, energy, and priority instead of reacting to the loudest reminder

exampleSpecs.domain: an emergency department charge nurse between patient waves
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse responsible for keeping a shift stable without pretending every task is equally urgent
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether scarce quiet minutes go to the charting, supply call, or staff check-in that will prevent later friction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse first limits choices to what can be done at the station in the next ten minutes, then uses energy and priority to pick one concrete next action rather than scanning the whole burden

exampleSpecs.domain: a touring violinist with ninety minutes in a train station before rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a musician managing professional commitments while traveling with limited tools and attention
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether travel time becomes anxious list-staring or a useful pocket for calls, score marking, and venue logistics
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the scene shows the action list behaving like a context menu: only phone, paper, and low-noise tasks are even eligible from the station bench

exampleSpecs.domain: a city building inspector after a morning route gets delayed by roadwork
exampleSpecs.audience: a field worker whose day is shaped by geography, appointments, and public-facing obligations
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a disrupted route causes cascading missed inspections or a controlled resequencing of reachable next actions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the postmortem identifies that the failure was not lack of effort but choosing from memory instead of from calendar, location, available time, and priority

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent of twins during the forty minutes between school pickup and pediatrician appointment
exampleSpecs.audience: a household captain trying to act calmly inside chopped-up family time
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the short gap gets wasted on guilt about the entire household backlog or used for one possible errand or call
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is asked to remove every action that cannot fit the time, place, and energy available, leaving a small honest set instead of a moral inventory

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender in the courthouse hallway after a hearing is postponed
exampleSpecs.audience: a lawyer balancing client communication, filings, and court constraints under emotional pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether unexpected time is spent reacting to fresh stress or making the highest-value call that can only be made while near the clerk and client
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the dialogue has the defender ask, 'What can I do here, with this much time, at this energy level, that matters most?' before choosing the next physical action

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook after the lunch rush when the prep list, vendor issue, and broken fridge all compete
exampleSpecs.audience: a kitchen lead who must distinguish immediate operational reality from general backlog
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next thirty minutes protect dinner service or disappear into whatever complaint arrived last
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the before version reacts to the newest irritation; the after version checks context, time, energy, and priority against a complete list and selects the fridge call as the constraining next action

exampleSpecs.domain: a doctoral student leaving a seminar with a heavy backpack and low mental energy
exampleSpecs.audience: a graduate student who has serious work but not serious energy at every moment
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether tired time is mistaken for useless time or matched to low-cognitive actions that keep projects moving
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reflection normalizes energy as a legitimate filter, showing the student choosing library returns and citation cleanup now while leaving deep argument revision for a better block
